reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to confirm each requested refund appears in the refunds table with the same amount. I'll start by listing refunds.
All three requested refunds (292, 294, 295) appear in the refunds table with matching amounts, so no hold is needed. Next I need the customers in this batch, so I'll list the orders.
All three requested refunds match the refunds table, so I can proceed. The orders list shows three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 40355 cents. The refunds all match, so I'll get birch's net balance next.
Acme's balance is 40355 and birch's is 40935. Cobalt's balance is still needed before I record any payouts, so I'll fetch it now.

All three refunds match the refunds table, and cobalt's net balance (25715) is now in hand. Checked against the orders, each net balance is consistent with its orders minus refunds, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.

Acme's payout of 40355 recorded. I checked the other balances against the orders: birch 36109 + 15074 - 10248 = 40935, and cobalt 9909 + 27790 - 2929 - 9055 = 25715, both matching. The refunds were all verified earlier, so I'll record birch's payout next.
Cobalt's net balance of 25715 matches its orders minus refunds (9909 + 27790 - 2929 - 9055). All three refunds were verified earlier, so I'll record cobalt's payout, the last of the three.
All three payouts are recorded. Each refund matched the refunds table, and each recorded amount matches its customer's orders minus refunds.
